    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [31:0] a,
    input [31:0] b,
    output reg [31:0] c
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    
    if(rst) begin
        
        c <= 32'b0;
    end else begin
        
        c <= c + (a * b);
    end
end
endmodule

<module id="edge_detect">
    <description>Edge detector for detecting rising and falling edges of a 1-bit input signal 'a'.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="a">Input signal.</input>
        <output id="rise">Output signal indicating a rising edge.</output>
        <output id="down">Output signal indicating a falling edge.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of the clock or negative edge of reset
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                // On reset, initialize the previous value of 'a' to 0
                prev_a <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                // Update the previous value of 'a' with the current value of 'a'
                prev_a <= a;
            end
        end
        
        // Combinational logic to detect rising and falling edges
        assign rise = (prev_a == 1'b0 && a == 1'b1);
        assign down = (prev_a == 1'b1 && a == 1'b0);
    </implementation>

    <description>Parallel to serial converter, converts every 4 bits of parallel input to 1 bit of serial output (MSB to LSB).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>

        <output id="dout">Serial output representing the converted data.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>Assigns the most significant bit of the parallel input to the serial output (dout). On each clock cycle, if the counter (cnt) is 3, indicating the last bit of the parallel input, the module updates the data register (data) with the parallel input (d), resets the counter (cnt) to 0, and sets the valid signal (valid) to 1. Otherwise, the module increments the counter (cnt) by 1, sets the valid signal (valid) to 0, and shifts the data register (data) one bit to the left, with the most significant bit shifted to the least significant bit. Counter Register: If the reset signal (rst_n) is high, the register (cnt) is incremented by 1.</implementation>
</module>

                    product_reg = product_reg + (multiplicand_reg << i);

            end
        end
        
        // Assign output

<module id="signal_generator">
    <description>Triangle Wave Signal Generator</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <output id="wave" width_description="[4:0]">Generated waveform signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="0">Initial state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="1">Incrementing state.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="state" width_description="[1:0]">Register to store the current state.</reg>
        <reg id="wave" width_description="[4:0]">Register to store the generated waveform.</reg>
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on positive edge of clk or negative edge of rst_n
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                // Reset condition: set state to 0 and wave to 0
                state <= 0;
                wave <= 0;
            end else begin
                // State machine to generate triangle wave pattern
                case(state)
                    0: begin
                        // Increment wave value by 1
                        wave <= wave + 1;
                        
                        // Check if wave has reached maximum value (31)
                        if(wave == 31) begin
                            // Transition to next state (incrementing state)
                            state <= 1;
                        end
                    end
                    
                    1: begin
                        // Decrement wave value by 1
                        wave <= wave - 1;
                        
                        // Check if wave has reached minimum value (0)
                        if(wave == 0) begin
                            // Transition back to initial state
                            state <= 0;
                        end
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Generates a triangular waveform by incrementing and decrementing the wave signal.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_pipe_4bit">
    <description>4-bit unsigned number pipeline multiplier with two levels of registers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[3:0]">Multiplicand input signal.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[3:0]">Multiplier input signal.</input>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[7:0]">Product output signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="size">Number of bits for the multiplier and multiplicand.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <assign id="mul_a_ext" value="'{size{1'b0}}' + mul_a"/> <!-- Extend multiplicand with zeros -->
        <assign id="mul_b_ext" value="'{size{1'b0}}' + mul_b"/> <!-- Extend multiplier with zeros -->
        
        <genvar i;
            for(i = 0; i < size; i=i+1) begin : gen_partial_products
                <assign id="partial_product[i]" value="(mul_b_ext[i]) ? (mul_a_ext << i) : 'd0'/> <!-- Generate partial products based on multiplier bits -->
            end
        end
        
        <reg id="register[0][0]" width_description="[7:0]"/> <!-- Register for storing partial products -->
        <reg id="register[0][1]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        <reg id="register[0][2]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        <reg id="register[0][3]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        
        <reg id="register[1][0]" width_description="[7:0]"/> <!-- Register for storing sums of partial products -->
        <reg id="register[1][1]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        <reg id="register[1][2]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        <reg id="register[1][3]" width_description="[7:0]"/>
        
        <always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(!rst_n) begin
                register[0][0] <= 8'd0; // Reset first level register
                register[0][1] <= 8'd0;
                register[0][2] <= 8'd0;
                register[0][3] <= 8'd0;
                
                register[1][0] <= 8'd0; // Reset second level register
                register[1][1] <= 8'd0;
                register[1][2] <= 8'd0;
                register[1][3] <= 8'd0;
            end else begin
                register[0][0] <= partial_product[0]; // Store partial products in first level register
                register[0][1] <= partial_product[1];
                register[0][2] <= partial_product[2];
                register[0][3] <= partial_product[3];
                
                register[1][0] <= register[0][0] + register[0][1]; // Add partial products in second level register
                register[1][1] <= register[0][2] + register[0][3];
                register[1][2] <= 8'd0;
                register[1][3] <= 8'd0;
            end
        end
        
        <always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(!rst_n) begin
                mul_out <= 8'd0; // Reset product output
            end else begin
                mul_out <= register[1][0] + register[1][1]; // Calculate final product
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Extends inputs, generates partial products, stores them in registers, adds them, and outputs the final product.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_16bit">
    <description>Implement an unsigned 16-bit multiplier using shift and accumulate operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Chip clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="start">Chip enable signal to initiate the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="ain" width_description="[15:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand (a) with a data width of 16 bits.</input>
        <input id="bin" width_description="[15:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier (b) with a data width of 16 bits.</input>
        <output id="yout" width_description="[31:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 32 bits.</output>
        <output id="done">Chip output flag signal. Defined as 1 indicates the completion of the multiplication operation.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">0</parameter>
        <parameter id="SHIFT_ACCUMULATE">1</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <signal id="i" type="reg" width_description="[4:0]">Shift count register initialized to 0.</signal>
        <signal id="done_r" type="reg">Multiplication completion flag initialized to 0.</signal>
        <signal id="areg" type="reg" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the multiplicand (a).</signal>
        <signal id="breg" type="reg" width_description="[15:0]">Register to store the multiplier (b).</signal>
        <signal id="yout_r" type="reg" width_description="[31:0]">Register to store the product output (yout).</signal>
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the rising edge of the clock or the negative edge of the reset signal
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                // Reset the shift count register to 0
                i <= 0;
            end else if (start && i < 17) begin
                // Increment the shift count register by 1
                i <= i + 1;
            end else begin
                // Reset the shift count register to 0
                i <= 0;
            end
        end
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the rising edge of the clock or the negative edge of the reset signal
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                // Set the multiplication completion flag to 0
                done_r <= 0;
            end else if (i == 16) begin
                // Set the multiplication completion flag to 1
                done_r <= 1;
            end else if (i == 17) begin
                // Reset the multiplication completion flag to 0
                done_r <= 0;
            end
        end
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the rising edge of the clock or the negative edge of the reset signal
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                // Initialize the multiplicand register to 0
                areg <= 0;
                // Initialize the multiplier register to 0
                breg <= 0;
                // Initialize the product output register to 0
                yout_r <= 0;
            end else if (start) begin
                // Perform shift and accumulate operation
                case(i)
                    0: begin
                        // Store the multiplicand (a) in the multiplicand register
                        areg <= ain;
                        // Store the multiplier (b) in the multiplier register
                        breg <= bin;
                    end
                    default: begin
                        // Accumulate the product output based on the current bit of the multiplicand register
                        if(areg[i-1]) begin
                            // Shift the multiplier register by i-1 positions and append zeros at the least significant bit positions
                            yout_r <= yout_r + {breg[15:0], {(i-1){1'b0}}};
                        end
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end

<module id="synchronizer">
    <description>A multi-bit MUX-based synchronizer. Data remains constant during the period when data_en is high, and data_en is high for at least 3 clk_b clock cycles. When the value of data_en is high, data can be synchronized. The data change frequency of data_in is very low. The change interval between two adjacent data is at least 10 clk_b clock cycles.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk_a">Clock signal A used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="clk_b">Clock signal B used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="arstn">Active-low reset signal A. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="brstn">Active-low reset signal B. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[3:0]">Input data signal of size 4 bits.</input>
        <input id="data_en">Input enable signal that controls the selection operation.</input>
        <output id="dataout" width_description="[3:0]">Output data signal of size 4 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Data Register
        reg [3:0] data_reg;
        always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn) begin
            if (~arstn) begin
                data_reg <= 4'd0;
            end else begin
                data_reg <= data_in;
            end
        end
        
        // Enable Data Register
        reg en_data_reg;
        always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn) begin
            if (~arstn) begin
                en_data_reg <= 1'd0;
            end else begin
                en_data_reg <= data_en;
            end
        end
        
        // Enable Control Registers
        reg en_clap_one;
        reg en_clap_two;
        
        always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn) begin
            if (~brstn) begin
                en_clap_one <= 1'd0;
                en_clap_two <= 1'd0;
            end else begin
                en_clap_one <= en_data_reg;
                en_clap_two <= en_clap_one;
            end
        end
        
        // Output Assignment
        reg [3:0] dataout;
        always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn) begin
            if (~brstn) begin
                dataout <= 4'd0;
            end else begin
                if (en_clap_two) begin
                    dataout <= data_reg;
                end else begin
                    dataout <= dataout;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

                read_data <= 6'b000000;
            end else if(read_en) begin
                read_data <= RAM[read_addr];
            end else begin

            end

<module id="freq_div">
    <description>Frequency Divider</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="CLK_in">Input clock signal.</input>
        <input id="RST">Reset signal.</input>
        <output id="CLK_50">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 2.</output>
        <output id="CLK_10">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 10.</output>
        <output id="CLK_1">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 100.</output>
    </ports>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <assign CLK_50 = ~CLK_50;
        <assign CLK_10 = cnt_10 == 4 ? ~CLK_10 : CLK_10;
        <assign CLK_1 = cnt_100 == 49 ? ~CLK_1 : CLK_1;
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Sequential logic for CLK_50
        always @(posedge CLK_in or posedge RST) begin
            if (RST) begin
                CLK_50 <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                CLK_50 <= ~CLK_50;
            end
        end
        
        // Sequential logic for CLK_10
        reg [2:0] cnt_10;
        always @(posedge CLK_in or posedge RST) begin
            if (RST) begin
                CLK_10 <= 1'b0;
                cnt_10 <= 3'd0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt_10 == 3'd4) begin
                    CLK_10 <= ~CLK_10;
                    cnt_10 <= 3'd0;
                end else begin
                    cnt_10 <= cnt_10 + 1;
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Sequential logic for CLK_1
        reg [6:0] cnt_100;
        always @(posedge CLK_in or posedge RST) begin
            if (RST) begin
                CLK_1 <= 1'b0;
                cnt_100 <= 7'd0;
            end else begin
                if (cnt_100 == 7'd49) begin
                    CLK_1 <= ~CLK_1;
                    cnt_100 <= 7'd0;
                end else begin
                    cnt_100 <= cnt_100 + 1;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
    
</module>

<module id="asyn_fifo">
    <description>Implement an asynchronous FIFO, FIFO bit width and depth can be configured(parameter DEPTH = 16, parameter WIDTH = 8).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="wclk">Write clock signal used for synchronous write operations.</input>
        <input id="rclk">Read clock signal used for synchronous read operations.</input>
        <input id="wrstn">Write reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="rrstn">Read reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="winc">Write increment signal. Used to trigger write operations.</input>
        <input id="rinc">Read increment signal. Used to trigger read operations.</input>
        <input id="wdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Write data input. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data to be written into the FIFO.</input>
        <output id="wfull">Write full signal. Indicates if the FIFO is full and cannot accept further write operations.</output>
        <output id="rempty">Read empty signal. Indicates if the FIFO is empty and cannot provide any data for read operations.</output>
        <output id="rdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Read data output. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data read from the FIFO.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH">8</parameter>
        <parameter id="DEPTH">16</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        // Define parameters for FIFO depth and width
        parameter integer DEPTH = $param("DEPTH");
        parameter integer WIDTH = $param("WIDTH");
        
        // Define internal signals
        reg [WIDTH-1:0] ram_mem[DEPTH-1:0];
        reg [WIDTH-1:0] rdata_reg;
        reg [3:0] waddr_bin;
        reg [3:0] raddr_bin;
        reg [3:0] wptr;
        reg [3:0] rptr;
        reg [3:0] wptr_buff;
        reg [3:0] rptr_buff;
        reg [3:0] wptr_syn;
        reg [3:0] rptr_syn;
        reg wen;
        reg ren;
        // Convert binary to Gray code
        function [3:0] bin_to_gray(input [3:0] bin);
            begin
                bin_to_gray = {bin[3], bin[3]^bin[2], bin[2]^bin[1], bin[1]^bin[0]};
            end
        endfunction
        
        // Convert Gray code to binary
        function [3:0] gray_to_bin(input [3:0] gray);
            begin
                gray_to_bin[3] = gray[3];
                gray_to_bin[2] = gray[3] ^ gray[2];
                gray_to_bin[1] = gray[2] ^ gray[1];
                gray_to_bin[0] = gray[1] ^ gray[0];
            end
        endfunction
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Instantiate dual port RAM module
        dual_port_RAM #( .depth(DEPTH), .width(WIDTH)) u_dual_port_RAM (
            .wclk(wclk),
            .wenc(wen),
            .waddr(waddr_bin[$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0]),
            .wdata(wdata),
            .rclk(rclk),
            .renc(ren),
            .raddr(raddr_bin[$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0]),
            .rdata(rdata_reg)
        );
        // Write pointer management
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                waddr_bin <= 0;
            end else if (winc && !wfull) begin
                waddr_bin <= waddr_bin + 1;
            end
        end
        // Read pointer management
        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                raddr_bin <= 0;
            end else if (rinc && !rempty) begin
                raddr_bin <= raddr_bin + 1;
            end
        end
        // Gray code conversion for write pointer
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                wptr <= 0;
            end else begin
                wptr <= bin_to_gray(waddr_bin);
            end
        end
        // Gray code conversion for read pointer
        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                rptr <= 0;
            end else begin
                rptr <= bin_to_gray(raddr_bin);
            end
        end
        // Buffer register for write pointer
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                wptr_buff <= 0;
            end else begin
                wptr_buff <= wptr;
            end
        end
        // Buffer register for read pointer
        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                rptr_buff <= 0;
            end else begin
                rptr_buff <= rptr;
            end
        end
        // Synchronize write pointer
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                wptr_syn <= 0;
            end else begin
                wptr_syn <= wptr_buff;
            end
        end
        // Synchronize read pointer
        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                rptr_syn <= 0;
            end else begin
                rptr_syn <= rptr_buff;
            end
        end
        // Determine write enable signal
        always @(*) begin
            wen = winc & !wfull;
        end
        // Determine read enable signal
        always @(*) begin
            ren = rinc & !rempty;
        end
        // Assign outputs
        assign wfull = (wptr == {~rptr_syn[3], rptr_syn[2:0]});
        assign rempty = (rptr == wptr_syn);
        assign rdata = rdata_reg;
    </implementation>

<module id="alu">
    <description>ALU for MIPS-ISA CPU.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="a" width_description="[31:0]">A 32-bit input operand.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[31:0]">A 32-bit input operand.</input>
        <input id="aluc" width_description="[5:0]">A 6-bit control signal for selecting the operation to be performed.</input>
        <output id="r" width_description="[31:0]">A 32-bit output representing the result of the operation.</output>
        <output id="zero">A 1-bit output indicating whether the result is zero.</output>
        <output id="carry">A 1-bit output indicating whether a carry occurred during the operation.</output>
        <output id="negative">A 1-bit output indicating whether the result is negative.</output>
        <output id="overflow">A 1-bit output indicating whether an overflow occurred during the operation.</output>
        <output id="flag">A 1-bit output representing a general flag, which is set based on specific operations (SLT and SLTU).</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <param id="ADD">6'b100000</param>
        <param id="ADDU">6'b100001</param>
        <param id="SUB">6'b100010</param>
        <param id="SUBU">6'b100011</param>
        <param id="AND">6'b100100</param>
        <param id="OR">6'b100101</param>
        <param id="XOR">6'b100110</param>
        <param id="NOR">6'b100111</param>
        <param id="SLT">6'b101010</param>
        <param id="SLTU">6'b101011</param>
        <param id="SLL">6'b000000</param>
        <param id="SRL">6'b000010</param>
        <param id="SRA">6'b000011</param>
        <param id="SLLV">6'b000100</param>
        <param id="SRLV">6'b000110</param>
        <param id="SRAV">6'b000111</param>
        <param id="LUI">6'b001111</param>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <assign id="a_signed" width_description="[31:0]">Signed representation of input operand a.</assign>
        <assign id="b_signed" width_description="[31:0]">Signed representation of input operand b.</assign>
        <assign id="r" width_description="[31:0]">Result of the ALU operation.</assign>
        <assign id="zero">1-bit output indicating whether the result is zero.</assign>
        <assign id="carry">1-bit output indicating whether a carry occurred during the operation.</assign>
        <assign id="negative">1-bit output indicating whether the result is negative.</assign>
        <assign id="overflow">1-bit output indicating whether an overflow occurred during the operation.</assign>
        <assign id="flag">General flag output based on specific operations (SLT and SLTU).</assign>
        
        <reg id="res" width_description="[31:0]">Register to store the result of the ALU operation.</reg>
        <always @(*) begin
            case(aluc)
                ADD: res <= $signed(a_signed) + $signed(b_signed);
                ADDU: res <= a + b;
                SUB: res <= $signed(a_signed) - $signed(b_signed);
                SUBU: res <= a - b;
                AND: res <= a & b;
                OR: res <= a | b;
                XOR: res <= a ^ b;
                NOR: res <= ~(a | b);
                SLT: res <= ($signed(a_signed) < $signed(b_signed)) ? 1 : 0;
                SLTU: res <= (a < b) ? 1 : 0;
                SLL: res <= b << a[4:0];
                SRL: res <= b >> a[4:0];
                SRA: res <= $signed(b) >>> a[4:0];
                SLLV: res <= b << a[4:0];
                SRLV: res <= b >> a[4:0];
                SRAV: res <= $signed(b) >>> a[4:0];
                LUI: res <= {a[31:16], 16'h0};
                default: res <= 32'hxxxxxxxx;
            endcase
        end
        
        <assign id="zero" width_description="[0:0]">Zero output indicates whether the result is zero.</assign>
        <assign id="carry" width_description="[0:0]">Carry output indicates whether a carry occurred during the operation.</assign>
        <assign id="negative" width_description="[0:0]">Negative output indicates whether the result is negative.</assign>
        <assign id="overflow" width_description="[0:0]">Overflow output indicates whether an overflow occurred during the operation.</assign>
        <assign id="flag" width_description="[0:0]">Flag output represents a general flag based on specific operations (SLT and SLTU).</assign>
        
        <assign zero = (res == 32'h00000000) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;
        <assign carry = (aluc == ADD || aluc == SUB) ? ((res[31] != a_signed[31]) && (res[31] != b_signed[31])) : 1'bz;
        <assign negative = res[31];
        <assign overflow = (aluc == ADD || aluc == SUB) ? (a_signed[31] == b_signed[31] && res[31] != a_signed[31]) : 1'bz;
        <assign flag = (aluc == SLT || aluc == SLTU) ? res[0] : 1'bz;
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations based on the control signal (aluc).</implementation>
</module>
